# Worker-default autosave ordering observation

This test-only fixture observes one essential engine fact before choosing a production preservation mechanism. It changes no existing research/prototype or MIR player file. Source role 0.1.0 must OMIT `migrations/0.1.1.lua`; target role 0.1.1 differs only by `info.version` and that read-only migration. Both use the exact current Factorio2.1 MIR5.0.21012 archive on2.1.23, with Base and this fixture only.

Three continuously supplied ordinary native labs run at authored speed3600 with zero force laboratory bonuses. Default worker4 retains its published675*1.5^(L-4),60-second/five-science/+1 contract. Player research advances from zero while two other forces advance effect-free sentinel work and retain queued27%/detached23% worker work. Prerequisites, foreign initial fractions, placement and supplies are explicitly scripted setup; no completed ordinary lab is claimed.

The source stores the exact native frame each tick and requests `game.auto_save` at nonround tick263. It never pauses the clock, disables labs, removes science or stops observing at the request. The target reads the serialized Lua frame and actual native state in a read-only Lua migration before configuration reconciliation, logs both, and requires exact native-state equality. No epsilon or one-tick allowance is permitted. A mismatch is an observed counterexample, not an expected-value adjustment or production failure. The target repeats observation during configuration before the one benchmark update.

The exact compared native frame contains each force's identity, aggregate bonus, current research, ordered queue, current fraction and public/sentinel/private level/researched/enablement/visibility/saved-work/count fields. Clock ticks and lab inventory/status/speed witnesses are emitted separately; they are not substituted for research work. Supplies are topped up before sampling when low, including after the save request, so research remains genuinely active.

The finite protocol is create, source server until the actual autosave is closed, and a separate target one-update benchmark using an immutable copied autosave: three processes,4GiB/180s/64MiB per process, existing governor/lease/archive restoration only. Root owns packaging, controller admission and execution. No native result exists merely because these files or host controls pass. Equality would qualify only this autosave/engine/input boundary, not every save trigger, multiplayer or a general per-tick design; the second engine remains separate.
